     1	# Server package agent rules
     2	
     3	Read root `AGENTS.md` first. This package owns the gateway, auth, connections, feeds, orchestration, connector operations, guardrails, Slackbot MCP integration, and embedded runtime.
     4	
     5	## Package-specific traps
     6	Read before editing. Full list in `docs/GOTCHAS.md`; these bite most often here:
     7	- This package is **biome-excluded**. Never run biome on it — edit surgically, matching each file's existing style. CI will not catch the reflow.
     8	- The DB client sets `fetch_types: false`, so a raw JS array bound as a parameter always fails. CI enforces this via `scripts/check-raw-array-params.mjs`; see GOTCHAS "DB & SQL" for the safe binding forms before reaching for a workaround.
     9	- Data-derived SQL `LIKE` prefixes must escape `\\`, `%`, and `_` and declare `ESCAPE '\\'`; prefer equality or an indexable range when possible. Identifiers such as Slack team ids legitimately contain `_`, so an unescaped prefix can cross tenant boundaries.
    10	- Hoisted `vi.mock()` silently fails in the integration suite (shared module registry). Use `vi.resetModules()` + `vi.doMock()` + dynamic import, and verify by co-running sibling test files.
    11	- Dropping a column from a queryable table is a two-phase change across two releases — `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` emits explicit column lists.
    12	
    13	## Boundaries and vocabulary
    14	- Connections are rows, not processes. Agents bind to connections/channels; replicas hydrate connection instances on demand from DB rows and must not assume boot warm-start.
    15	- Connectors collect external data into feeds/events; chat platforms deliver conversations/messages. Do not blur connector sync with chat transport.
    16	- Behaviors are the UI umbrella: Listen, Watch, Schedule. A watcher owns windows; a window's living state is a canvas (`semantic_type='canvas_state'`). Artifacts are stored files, not watcher state.
    17	- Platform isolation: InteractionService events carry `platform`; each renderer filters on its own platform and never another's.
    18	
    19	## Connections, feeds, and routing
    20	- Chat platforms live under `src/gateway/connections/` and use Chat SDK adapters. Configure connections via `/agents` UI or CRUD API; do not add per-platform env vars or bespoke SDK transports.
    21	- Webhooks are the default transport. Telegram alone supports `auto|webhook|polling`; reject polling in cloud mode.
    22	- `feeds` is the unified list. `kind='collected'` feeds are scheduled connector pulls into `events`; `kind='streaming'` feeds are chat channels backed by `channel_messages`, not scheduled syncs; `virtual` feeds are projections/metadata and must not be queued as real sync work.
    23	- Runtime connection ids may be slugs/managed ids (for example `slackinst-…`), not numeric `connections.id`. Resolve through connection stores; do not cast runtime ids to bigint.
    24	- Bound chat channels should materialize an idempotent streaming feed so the UI has one feed model, not a separate channel island.
    25	
    26	## Auth, providers, and secrets
    27	- Product auth uses better-auth/session/PAT flows in `src/auth`; model/provider auth and user auth profiles live under `src/gateway/auth`.
    28	- Provider catalog/settings are org/user scoped. Do not hardcode provider credentials, base URLs, or model lists; resolve through the provider catalog/settings stores.
    29	- Workers never see real credentials. The gateway secret/MCP proxies swap placeholders or inject OAuth/API credentials at egress.
    30	- MCP servers come from per-agent settings or `SKILL.md`; workers discover tools at startup and call them through the gateway proxy.
    31	- Device-pinned connectors are special: resolved connection credentials may be delivered only to the authorized device worker that owns that run.
    32	- Connector-contributed agent tooling (`gateway/agent-tooling/`) is the other carve-out, and only for **leases**: a short-lived provider-derived token (GitHub App installation tokens, ~1h) minted per deployment and injected as a real env var. It expires on its own and is revocable at the provider without touching the stored credential, which never leaves the gateway. `credential: 'lease'` is the only tier — there is deliberately no static-credential tier, because the worker egress proxy raw-tunnels HTTPS CONNECT and cannot swap a placeholder inside TLS; a CLI would send the placeholder to the provider verbatim. Any other tier value is dropped, not defaulted. Never widen this to a durable stored credential.
    33	
    34	  **Lifecycle limitation (v1):** a lease is minted at deployment time and the worker reads its env once at process start, so a WARM deployment keeps the credential it was born with. On a conversation that stays continuously active past the token's ~1h life, `gh` starts reporting itself unauthenticated; a connector connected mid-conversation likewise does not appear until the worker is rebuilt. Bounded by `WORKER_IDLE_CLEANUP_MINUTES` (default 60): any hour-long idle gap reaps the worker and the next turn mints fresh. Recycling a deployment before its lease or tooling goes stale is tracked separately — it is a concurrency-sensitive change (teardown must not interrupt a live turn, and the message path only sees deployments its own pod owns), which is why it is not folded in here. Credentials, egress domains, and declared nix packages reach EVERY runtime: remote runtimes provision the packages from the signed `nixPackages` claim via the provider's optional `ensurePackages` (see the nix bullet under "Guardrails, network, and runtime"). A provider that implements no `ensurePackages` is the one case that still gets the credential plus whatever tools its image ships.
    35	
    36	## Multi-replica correctness
    37	- Production can run N>1 replicas. Before claiming a feature works, ask: “does this hold with 3 replicas?” Correctness must not depend on session affinity.
    38	- Per-pod state (`SseManager`, event backlog, in-process worker map, deploy-lock cache) is pod-local. Cross-replica delivery must use Postgres (`thread_response` queue or equivalent).
    39	- API/SSE terminal rows and interaction cards are owner-routed; non-owners requeue until the owning pod claims. Headless rows with no SSE client may be delivered by first claim.
    40	- Streaming deltas/status are best-effort across pods today. Do not build correctness on cross-pod in-memory delivery.
    41	- Exclusive transports such as Telegram polling run on exactly one replica via `connection_claims`; webhook transports must run on any replica.
    42	
    43	## Durable dispatch and coordination
    44	- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed, deliver, or skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows are failures, not "nothing changed".
    45	- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check. Re-derive where the decision belongs, and put it at the chokepoint that already serializes the action — worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod. Prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over a hand-rolled hold/requeue.
    46	- **Interactive browser drafts are page-activated, never tab-pushed.** Persist the draft operation and its normal Lobu notification; the generic Chrome extension badges exact pending URLs and activates the run only when the user visits one in a user-owned tab. Extension and server core carry no connector, Behavior, selector, or site-specific rules — connector/reaction code owns URL shapes and page interaction. Never auto-submit. Only scrape-owned scratch tabs may be opened and closed automatically.
    47	
    48	## Connector operations and feed health
    49	- Built-in connector definitions/catalog install in server; connector implementation details belong in `packages/connectors/AGENTS.md`.
    50	- The active `connector_definitions` row is capability truth. Definitions may come from bundled source, organization-scoped `connector_versions`, or device manifests, so a grep under `packages/connectors` cannot prove an action is absent; inspect the active row and `operations.listAvailable`.
    51	- Organization-scoped compiled code shadows the shared artifact for the active version. `refreshConnectorDefinitions` skips keys with no bundled source, but re-syncs every active key that does have bundled source and can reset its definition version/schema to bundled metadata; inspect the active definition after deploy instead of assuming an override survived.
    52	- A data connection's `device_worker_id` is scrape affinity, not evidence that the browser is in front of the user. Connector-initiated browser actions currently inherit that pin. Until an interactive flow carries an explicit Chrome connection, a `completed` action proves execution on the selected extension, not that the user can see it; verify the resolved Chrome connection/worker before claiming delivery.
    53	- Connector health scans `connections` + `feeds`; chat connections are not collector connections and should not trip zero-feed collector health rules.
    54	- Feed hard auto-pause emits `feed.auto_paused` (Behavior signal + lifecycle event). Prefer a normal Behavior over new special-case agent subsystems.
    55	
    56	## Guardrails, network, and runtime
    57	- Guardrails live under `packages/core/src/guardrails/`; server built-ins/aggregation live under gateway guardrail code. Guardrail infra errors fail open; each trip writes a `guardrail-trip` event.
    58	- Worker HTTP(S) egress goes through the authenticated gateway proxy plus `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`/`WORKER_DISALLOWED_DOMAINS`. The proxy binds `127.0.0.1` **by design** — the Linux `IPAddressDeny=any` / `IPAddressAllow=127.0.0.1` scope depends on it, so do not make the host configurable. The port comes from `WORKER_PROXY_PORT` (default 8118); consume the injected `HTTP_PROXY` URL rather than rebuilding it.
    59	- Embedded workers are subprocesses under `./workspaces/{agentId}/` with `WORKSPACE_DIR`. Linux hosts with a usable user systemd wrap them in `systemd-run --user --scope`; other hosts run them unwrapped unless `LOBU_REQUIRE_WORKER_SANDBOX=1`.
    60	- Nix packages (agent + connector-contributed, unioned at resolve time; legacy skill-level packages are ignored) are portable across runtimes. The built-in runtime wraps the worker spawn in `nix-shell -p`; remote runtimes get the same set as the SIGNED `nixPackages` worker-token claim and `/internal/runtime/exec` provisions it via the provider's optional `ensurePackages` before the first command. Rules when touching this: the list comes from the token claim and NEVER the request body (same as `allowedDomains` — the worker is the sandbox-ee); every name goes through `nixPackageAttrRef` before it reaches a command line; idempotence is a marker file in the sandbox filesystem, never a gateway Map (another replica handles the next message); and provisioning degrades honestly — a failed install or a provider with no `ensurePackages` leaves the CLI absent and says so in the exec result, it never fails the turn. Remote provisioning needs the nix substituter hosts in the sandbox network policy, added gateway-side only when there is a validated package set.
    61	
    62	## Local dev and validation
    63	- Prereqs: Bun, supported Node per package engines, and Postgres+pgvector via `DATABASE_URL`. `./scripts/setup-dev.sh` provisions local Postgres where needed.
    64	- `make dev` uses shared brew Postgres with one DB per branch. `LOBU_EMBEDDED=1 make dev` / `make dev-embedded` uses embedded per-worktree Postgres.
    65	- Parallel worktrees use `.env.local` for non-default `PORT`/`WORKER_PROXY_PORT`; do not `git switch` while a dev server runs. Read your worktree's `PORT` from `.env.local` — it is not 8787.
    66	- Smoke a booted server: `curl -s localhost:$PORT/api/health` (readiness is `/health/ready`). The SPA is pathless at `:$PORT`; the agent API is under `:$PORT/lobu`. "It booted" is not "it works" — drive the path you changed.
    67	- Validation: the root gates (see root `AGENTS.md`) plus the relevant server `bun test` / `make test-integration` suites.
    68	
    69	## Slackbot MCP integration
    70	- Slackbot is an MCP client. A Slack app exposes tools/resources only with `mcp:connect` bot scope plus an `mcp_servers` manifest block; after scope changes, reinstall the app.
    71	- Manifest template: `config/slack-app-manifest.self-install.json`. Manage it with `scripts/slack-manifest.ts` (`print|validate|update`) and Slack config credentials.
    72	- `/mcp` is mounted at app root, not under `/lobu`. Manifest MCP URL is `<origin>/mcp`; webhook/slash/OAuth URLs keep the `/lobu` base. Do not change this to `/lobu/mcp`.
    73	- `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is the canonical web/OAuth origin advertised in protected-resource metadata. MCP `WWW-Authenticate` resource metadata uses the request host when it is the configured origin or belongs to `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`; otherwise it falls back to `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL`. For Slack cloud flows these must resolve to public HTTPS origins; update env and restart when switching origins.
    74	- Local public dev endpoint is Tailscale Funnel to gateway `:8787`; verify `/mcp` returns auth challenge, not 404.

     1	# Connector authorization & data attribution model
     2	
     3	> **Status (2026-07-15):** **Open RFC** — no implementation; attribution work so far is per-connector, not this org-backbone model.
     4	
     5	Status: design / RFC. Builds on `authz-acl-permission-program.md` (the access-graph
     6	engine + fail-closed resource-visibility gate, already live for Slack + GitHub) and
     7	`feeds-and-connections-model.md`.
     8	
     9	## Problem
    10	
    11	For team/work tools (Jira, Linear, GitHub, Slack), we have to decide how a connector
    12	is authorized and how its data is attributed to users:
    13	
    14	- **Per-user**: each user authorizes their own account; we only ever see their slice.
    15	  Simple permissions, but no shared picture and no cross-user reasoning.
    16	- **Org scrape + attribute**: an admin connects once, we ingest the full picture, and
    17	  each user only sees the subset they're allowed to see in the source tool.
    18	
    19	Decided requirements (from product):
    20	
    21	1. The agent must answer **both** personal ("my tickets") and org-wide ("sprint status,
    22	   who's blocked") questions.
    23	2. Setup is **admin once, with optional per-user** connections layered on.
    24	3. Visibility is a **strict mirror, fail-closed** of the source tool's own permissions.
    25	4. Whether we need data the admin token can't see (private/restricted) is **undecided**.
    26	
    27	## How Claude / ChatGPT connectors do it (reference point)
    28	
    29	They use **pure per-user OAuth + live retrieval**. You add a connector, authorize it with
    30	your own account, and at query time the model calls the remote MCP server **with your
    31	token**. Access is **delegated to the source** — you see exactly what your token can see,
    32	enforced by Jira/GitHub, not by the assistant. There is **no central scrape**, so there is
    33	**nothing to attribute**: every request already runs as the asking user.
    34	
    35	The cost of that simplicity is exactly the capability Lobu exists to provide: a shared,
    36	persistent, cross-user picture. The moment you keep a central copy you inherit the
    37	attribution problem Claude designed around. **The ACL mirror is the price of the shared
    38	corpus** — you cannot have Lobu's shared memory *and* Claude's "no attribution needed."
    39	
    40	## How Glean / Copilot do it (the org-backbone reference point)
    41	
    42	Glean is the canonical "org backbone + ACL mirror" product, and it shows the identity step
    43	done well: the **admin** connects each source once and Glean crawls everything, mirroring
    44	each document's **ACL** into the index. The **user logs in once via SSO** — never to the
    45	individual tools. Identity is **federated from a shared corporate IdP** (Okta/Google/Azure
    46	AD): the SSO assertion gives an *authoritative, verified* email/subject, and because every
    47	source sits behind that same IdP, "this user = this Jira accountId = this GitHub SAML
    48	identity" is a SCIM directory lookup, not a guess. Microsoft Copilot does the same via
    49	Azure AD/Graph.
    50	
    51	Takeaway: requiring users to log into every tool individually is *more* friction than Glean
    52	and is only necessary when there is **no** shared IdP. "Email match" is risky only when
    53	*guessed*; from a verified SSO assertion it is authoritative — that is the whole trick.
    54	
    55	## Recommended model: org backbone + ACL mirror + per-user overlay
    56	
    57	A superset of Claude's model:
    58	
    59	- **Ingest (full picture)** — admin installs one connection per source (GitHub App,
    60	  Jira/Linear OAuth, broad scope). Everything that install can see lands in `events`.
    61	- **Gate (per-user, fail-closed)** — the existing `authz/*` layer attributes visibility:
    62	  map each Lobu user → their source identity; sync source membership (repos/projects/teams)
    63	  on a cron; `resource-visibility` shows an event iff the user is `member_of` its resource;
    64	  unknown/stale membership → hidden. "Both" falls out for free — org-wide is the same gate
    65	  for a user whose membership spans the org; "my tickets" is the same gate filtered to one
    66	  person. One mechanism, not two code paths.
    67	- **Overlay (optional per-user)** — a user connects their own account to reach what the
    68	  admin token can't (restricted projects, private repos/DMs). Ingests tagged to them; the
    69	  gate naturally shows it only to them. This sub-path **is** Claude's model.
    70	
    71	### Phasing
    72	
    73	- **P1 — per-user (Claude-style).** Per-user connect via `manage_connections` (already
    74	  returns `connect_url`; the agent sends it in chat). Source-enforced, zero new ACL work.
    75	  Safe default for any source, and the only viable mode for personal sources (Gmail, bank).
    76	- **P2 — org backbone + gate, per source.** Admin org connection + an ACL sync + a
    77	  `sources.ts` entry + the connector stamping the resource id. Per the authz program, a new
    78	  source is "1 `sources.ts` entry + connector stamp, no gate/engine change."
    79	- **P3 — per-user overlay for gaps.** Only build per source when a real private-data gap
    80	  bites (resolves requirement #4: don't speculate).
    81	
    82	### In-chat "needs auth" UX
    83	
    84	P1: the agent just sends the `connect_url` as a message (no new infra; reliable because
    85	it's a normal assistant turn). Later: reuse `postLinkButton` (the `oauth` linkType already
    86	exists and rides owner-routed delivery) for a button affordance. Do **not** reuse
    87	`status-message:created` (wrong semantics; currently orphaned).
    88	
    89	For a **not-logged-in** user the connect step *is* the identity step: the OAuth round-trip
    90	both authenticates them and links their source identity. An unlinked user has no membership
    91	→ fail-closed → sees nothing → the agent prompts "sign in here to connect."
    92	
    93	## Gaps & open questions
    94	
    95	Ordered by how much they threaten the stated requirements.
    96	
    97	1. **Identity link in pure-backbone mode (the model's structural hole).** The gate needs an
    98	   authoritative Lobu-user → source-identity mapping. In backbone mode the user never
    99	   connects their own account, so there's no OAuth to prove the link. Options: admin-provided
   100	   mapping (SCIM/CSV), a grant-nothing "verify your GitHub" OAuth, or directory email-match
   101	   (risky — wrong mapping over-shares). **Must not guess by email.** This is the prerequisite
   102	   the backbone model doesn't supply on its own.
   103	
   104	2. **Granularity mismatch vs "strict mirror" (req #3).** The gate is resource-membership
   105	   (repo/project). Sources have finer ACLs: issue-level restrictions, Jira field-level
   106	   security, private comments, confidential issues, draft PRs. Repo/project membership is
   107	   **coarser than the source**, so a project member could see a restricted issue they
   108	   couldn't see in Jira — which violates "strict mirror." Either ingest the finer ACL
   109	   (expensive) or consciously accept coarser-than-source and downgrade the promise to
   110	   "resource-level mirror."
   111	
   112	3. **Derived-data leakage.** Per-event gating is not enough. Summaries, embeddings, entity
   113	   fields, watcher outputs, and `metric_layer` rollups computed over the full corpus can leak
   114	   restricted info to a user who can't see the underlying events. Derived/aggregate layers
   115	   need the same gate (or per-audience computation), or they're a side channel.
   116	
   117	4. **Write-back = confused deputy.** Reads can use the backbone, but **actions** (create
   118	   issue, comment, merge) must run as the user, not the admin token — otherwise the agent
   119	   performs writes the user isn't allowed to make. Strongly implies the per-user overlay (P3)
   120	   is required for *writes* even where reads use the backbone. Decide: block writes without
   121	   per-user creds, or require overlay for any write.
   122	
   123	5. **Partial org-wide results.** A user not in every project gets a rollup of only their
   124	   accessible subset. Does the agent silently return a partial "sprint status," or disclose
   125	   "limited to what you can access"? Silent truncation is a correctness/trust issue.
   126	
   127	6. **Revocation latency.** Membership syncs on a cron (e.g. */15). Between a source-side
   128	   permission removal and the next sync there's a window. Fail-closed handles *unknown*
   129	   membership (over-hide, safe) but a freshly-*revoked* user may still see data until resync.
   130	   Document the SLA; consider event-driven invalidation for high-sensitivity sources.
   131	
   132	7. **Concentration of risk.** The org backbone makes a central copy of potentially very
   133	   sensitive data whose only protection is the gate. A gate bug → mass leak. Minimize ingest
   134	   scope, encrypt at rest, audit recall. The blast radius is strictly larger than Claude's
   135	   per-user model.
   136	
   137	8. **Sources without an ACL API.** The gate needs a queryable membership/ACL source
   138	   (GitHub collaborators, `conversations.members`). Webhook/email/CSV feeds expose none →
   139	   fail-closed (nobody sees anything) or org-wide-visible (violates strict mirror). Per-source
   140	   decision.
   141	
   142	9. **Backbone + overlay dedup.** If both the org backbone and a user's overlay ingest the
   143	   same resource, events double-count in memory/metrics. Cross-path dedup (different
   144	   connection sources, same upstream object) is new vs the existing single-path advisory-lock
   145	   dedup.
   146	
   147	10. **Scrape cost/scale.** Full-org history ingest is expensive (storage + embeddings; see
   148	    prior embed-backfill incidents). May need selective/lazy/recent-window ingest rather than
   149	    "scrape everything."
   150	
   151	11. **"Empty" disambiguation for UX.** The agent should distinguish "empty because you have
   152	    no access" from "empty because there's no data," to give a useful message (prompt connect
   153	    vs say nothing found).
   154	
   155	## Decisions made (2026-06-29)
   156	
   157	- **D1 — Identity link: hybrid (IdP-federated + verify-OAuth fallback).** SSO orgs federate
   158	  identity from the verified SSO assertion + SCIM (Glean-style, login once); no-SSO/personal
   159	  accounts fall back to one-click per-source verify-OAuth (Claude-style). Authoritative in
   160	  both modes — never email-guessing. Slots into the existing `$member` identity collapse
   161	  (`auth:signup` identity).
   162	- **D2 — ACL fidelity: resource-level, upgrade per source.** Ship repo/project-membership
   163	  gating now (reuses the engine); tighten to sub-resource only where a source needs it. The
   164	  promise is "resource-level mirror," tightened per source — not a blanket "exactly matches
   165	  the source." High-sensitivity sources needing sub-resource fidelity are candidates to stay
   166	  per-user (Claude-style) instead of joining the backbone.
   167	- **D3 — Writes: require per-user creds.** Reads may come from the backbone, but any action
   168	  (create/comment/merge) runs as the user's connected account. No admin-token writes
   169	  (confused-deputy). Implies the per-user overlay is a prerequisite for write-enabled tools.
   170	- **D4 — Partial results: disclose when likely incomplete.** The gate must emit a "rows were
   171	  filtered" signal; the agent flags "limited to what you can access" only when it fires.
   172	  Requires a filtered-count signal out of `resource-visibility`.
   173	- **D5 — First source: GitHub.** Repo-collaborator ACL sync already exists; resource = repo;
   174	  GitHub App = clean org backbone. Lowest new work, best end-to-end proof of P2.
   175	
   176	### Identity & login — what ships today (no enterprise layer needed)
   177	
   178	The D1 identity link works on the OSS path now: better-auth `genericOAuth` + built-in
   179	`socialProviders`, credential-resolved **per org** (an org can use its own OAuth app). So
   180	"log in with your company Google/GSuite (or GitHub, or any OIDC provider) and see only your
   181	data" works today — the access decision uses the user's *verified* login identity + the
   182	**source's own ACL** (GitHub collaborators, Slack channels). No SCIM or directory sync is
   183	required for a connector vertical.
   184	
   185	The enterprise identity layer — SAML, SCIM provisioning, enforced/domain-routed SSO, and
   186	IdP-group→access federation — is intentionally **kept out of this OSS core** and speced
   187	separately as a closed layer (owletto `docs/enterprise-idp-rfc.md`). It plugs in via the
   188	existing seams (the better-auth `plugins` array + the authz `sources.ts` registry) without
   189	forking core, and is additive — verticals ship on the path above first.
   190	
   191	### Implied next steps
   192	1. GitHub P2 vertical: org-App backbone connection + confirm repo ACL sync feeds the gate +
   193	   connector stamps repo resource id (per the authz program, mostly wiring an existing path).
   194	2. Identity: SSO/SCIM-federated identity link (D1) + verify-OAuth fallback; map onto `$member`.
   195	3. Gate signal for D4 (filtered-count) surfaced to the worker for disclosure.
   196	4. Write path (D3): per-user-cred requirement enforced at the connector-operation layer.
   197	5. Derived-data gating (gap #3) and backbone/overlay dedup (gap #9) before scaling beyond
   198	   one source.

payload.message: Two important fractures are already clear. First, `origin/main` does not have event-driven Slack revocation: the production path is periodic `conversations.members` reconciliation, and there is no `member_left_channel` handler. Second, the proposed connector-only denylist is not a security boundary because `$links` currently accepts any visible relationship-type slug. I’m now checking multi-writer ownership, merge behavior, and whether “six writers” is itself complete.

content.text: Two important fractures are already clear. First, `origin/main` does not have event-driven Slack revocation: the production path is periodic `conversations.members` reconciliation, and there is no `member_left_channel` handler. Second, the proposed connector-only denylist is not a security boundary because `$links` currently accepts any visible relationship-type slug. I’m now checking multi-writer ownership, merge behavior, and whether “six writers” is itself complete.

    94	
    95	Ordered by how much they threaten the stated requirements.
    96

    99	3. **Freshness:** the source's `freshness_state = fresh` — checked **inside the
   100	   gate SQL**, so missing/unknown/stale ACL state DENIES in the same query.
   101	
   102	Viewer closure = `$member` + trusted source identities + transitive `member_of`
   103	(recursive CTE; materialized closure later) + org/public audiences. Returns
   104	visible resource ids → filters `channel_messages` / `events`. Applied uniformly:
   105	`search.ts` recall, RAG, agent tool-calls, feeds route, exports — no bypass.
   106	**Do NOT simply replace the agent-bound-channel fence with the user gate** — that
   107	widens access from "agent's channels" to "all the user's channels"; intersect them.
   108	
   109	## 5. Freshness / revocation
   110	Per-source `freshness_state` (fresh|stale|unknown|failed) + `aclSupport`
   111	(full|partial|none) + `strict_mode`. Membership removals are high-priority
   112	invalidation (Slack `member_left_channel`, already-subscribed events + reconcile
   113	job). Bounded SLA (Slack private <30s target; others <1-5min); fail closed when
   114	stale/unknown. Storage: a small `authz_source_acl_state` (org, connection) — the
   115	ONE genuinely-new small table besides provenance.
   116	
   117	## 6. Derived-artifact ACLs (AI oversharing)
   118	`derived_artifact_sources(artifact_event_id, source_event_id)` provenance; an
   119	artifact (summary/embedding/memory/cached answer) is visible iff the viewer can
   120	see ALL its sources. Provenance must be **complete + transitive**; **missing,
   121	deleted, stale, or unknown-ACL source → DENY the artifact** (fail closed — partial
   122	provenance is not visibility). RAG: filter candidates → build prompt → revalidate
   123	citations.
   124	
   125	## 7. Database changes (minimal — this is the consolidation payoff)
   126	- `entity_identities`: add `assurance` (+ `verified_at`), two-phase (squawk gate).
   127	  [extends existing table]
   128	- `authz_source_acl_state`: small per-(org,connection) freshness/strict-mode row. [new, small]
   129	- `derived_artifact_sources`: provenance for derived artifacts. [new, small]
   130	- `can_read` + `deny_read` relationship types: **data, no migration** (runtime `ensure*Type`).
   131	- Channels/workspaces as entities, memberships, ACL edges: **no migration** (reuse).
   132	
   133	Net: **1 column add + 2 small tables** — vs. the 5 new tables the from-scratch
   134	approach implied.
   135	
   136	## 8. SDK shape (extends ConnectorRuntime; Okta = a connector, no IdP subsystem)
   137	Connectors emit a typed record union during sync: `event` (today) + `acl`
   138	(per-item, boolean expr) + `principal` + `membership` + `identity`; declare
   139	`provides[]` + `aclSupport`. **Okta** = `provides:['principals','groups','identity']`,
   140	no feeds. **Slack** = event + acl(membership) + principals/groups + identity.
   141	Per-connector ACL compiler = the trusted security boundary (test suites + golden
   142	fixtures + "unsupported feature ⇒ fail closed").

## Verdict

Bluntly: **the third recommendation is still wrong as written**, although it is substantially closer.

The remaining structural errors are:

1. It removes relationship-claim state without replacing it.
2. It places the ACL protection at the connector-rule layer instead of the shared relationship write boundary.
3. “Migrate all six writers” is an incomplete mutation inventory.
4. It does not cover column security or feedless directory synchronization.
5. `channel-about` is not an isolated overwrite bug; it is proof that one logical edge can have multiple independent owners.

The locked architecture explicitly requires the existing graph, effective principals, deny-wins, user ∩ agent, freshness, and all-source derived provenance ([authz plan §§1, 3–8](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:26)). The connector-authz document is explicitly an open RFC and itself admits field-level, derived-data, revocation, and cross-connection dedupe gaps ([connector model §Gaps](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/connector-authz-model.md:93)).

Also, do not confuse the locked target with the current implementation:

- `can_read|deny_read` has zero package occurrences.
- The current gate directly tests `member_of`, and never-graphed connections pass through ([resource-visibility.ts:86](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/authz/resource-visibility.ts:86)).
- `SyncResult` contains only events/checkpoint/auth metadata ([connector-types.ts:870](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/connector-sdk/src/connector-types.ts:870)).
- Derived provenance is documented as pending, not implemented ([authz plan §6](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:117)).

## A. Judgment on the six recommendations

1. **Drop the separate claims table:** conditionally right. You may drop the table, but not claim semantics. With the current live-triple uniqueness, your design cannot represent two independent assertions.

2. **Drop reserved-type tiers:** only if you retain one unforgeable distinction: trusted security compiler versus every generic writer. A broad tier taxonomy is unnecessary; central protection of `member_of`, `can_read`, and `deny_read` is mandatory.

3. **Fix `channel-about`:** yes, but not with a localized “don’t overwrite source” patch. Its upsert replaces both `source` and metadata ([channel-about.ts:257](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/authz/channel-about.ts:257)). Config and manual assertions need to coexist. `DO NOTHING` would merely make whichever assertion arrived first impossible to retract correctly.

4. **One relationship-store chokepoint:** yes. But migrate all mutators, not merely the six insert paths. Current additional mutations include merge collision tombstoning/repointing ([entity-merge.ts:286](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:286)), tool unlink/update ([manage_entity.ts:1574](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:1574)), and force-delete hard deletion ([entity-management.ts:1027](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:1027)).

5. **Connector domain/knowledge rules only:** right separation, incomplete mechanism. The protected-type check must be in the relationship store, not merely in connector validation. Rules also need stable assertion identity, update/retraction semantics, resolved endpoint roles, batching, and transaction propagation.

6. **Let authz proceed separately:** correct as project separation, but both programs must share the same protected relationship store and connector trust mechanism. Otherwise domain infrastructure becomes an ACL bypass.

One more issue: `buildAccessGraph` is described as atomic by its callers, but it accepts no transaction, obtains its own DB client, writes edges incrementally, and marks freshness afterward ([access-graph.ts:280](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/authz/access-graph.ts:280), [access-graph.ts:378](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/authz/access-graph.ts:378)). Slack invokes it once per team. The final design needs one per-connection transaction, with freshness set only after the entire reconcile commits.

## B. The 12 use cases

| # | Verdict | Stress-test result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. ERP graph | **Needs missing semantics** | Five fixed hops and 400 entity types are not inherently a problem if writes are batched and indexed. But current `belongs_to` is only an event-to-entity attribution role, not an entity edge ([connector-types.ts:559](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/connector-sdk/src/connector-types.ts:559)). A relationship rule needs named resolved endpoints and a stable assertion key. On invoice reassignment or source deletion it must retract/move the old assertion. Do not infer ACLs by walking the five domain hops. |
| 2. Slack private membership | **Locked design holds; current code does not** | The periodic full reconcile exists, but there is no fast `member_left_channel` path. The bot event list contains `member_joined_channel` but not `member_left_channel` ([slack.ts:64](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:64)), contradicting the plan’s “already-subscribed” claim in §5. A high-priority source-scoped retraction plus periodic reconcile is required. |
| 3. Jira intersection | **Holds with compiler** | Your core claim is correct: two `can_read` edges mean A OR B under an existential gate. Jira’s A AND B must become concrete effective members or a synthetic intersection principal, exactly as locked in §3 ([authz plan:84](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:84)). |
| 4. Row-level region access | **Holds** | Attach each customer event to an explicit ACL resource—often one region `$resource`—and write `resource can_read region-principal`, with reps `member_of` that principal. Domain `customer belongs_to region` must not itself confer access. |
| 5. Column-level invoice amount | **Breaks outright** | A row-level edge gates the whole event. A mask applied only after row authorization is too late if the value has already entered search text, embeddings, prompts, summaries, exports, caches, or logs. The connector RFC explicitly identifies field-level security as beyond the resource gate ([connector model:104](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/connector-authz-model.md:104)). Simplest safe representation: store `total_amount` as a separate finance-only child event/facet and omit it from the base invoice event. Otherwise you need a genuine field-projection subsystem. |
| 6. Agent `$links` | **Breaks outright** | The tool accepts any visible relationship-type slug, validates shape/scope, and inserts it ([manage_entity.ts:1463](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:1463)). With the current gate consuming `member_of`, that is an ACL-forging path. A connector-only denylist does nothing here. |
| 7. Auto-linker mentions | **Holds after store migration** | `mentions` at confidence 0.4 is appropriate domain evidence and must never participate in authorization closure. The current SELECT-then-INSERT is racy ([auto-linker.ts:111](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/auto-linker.ts:111)); the store should use atomic assertion upsert and retain event provenance. |
| 8. Derived summary over three events | **Locked design holds; unbuilt** | It must be visible only if all three source versions are visible, with complete transitive provenance and fail-closed missing/stale sources ([authz plan §6](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:117)). This is not an ordinary OR edge. |
| 9. Public-catalog reference | **Holds for domain edges** | Existing validation correctly requires the source entity to be tenant-owned and allows only the target to belong to a public catalog ([relationship-validation.ts:58](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/relationship-validation.ts:58)). Security edges should be same-org only; a public target must never become an ACL bridge. |
| 10. Entity merge | **Breaks without claim-aware merge** | Current merge tombstones any loser edge that would collide with a winner triple, preserving logical reachability but discarding independent ownership/provenance ([entity-merge.ts:286](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:286)). Claim-granular rows must survive as separate assertions; self-loops alone are discarded. |
| 11. Same edge from two connectors | **Breaks outright** | The current unique index permits one live row per triple ([baseline schema:3723](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:3723)). If A and B both assert the edge, retracting A cannot know B still supports it. `source` is a single text field, not multi-owner state ([baseline schema:1204](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1204)). |
| 12. Feedless Okta/SCIM | **Breaks current connector lifecycle** | The locked plan requires it, but today `ConnectorRuntime.sync()` is feed-oriented and returns `SyncResult`; no-feed integration connectors deliberately throw if polled ([connector-runtime.ts:56](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/connector-sdk/src/connector-runtime.ts:56), [connector-runtime.ts:199](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/connector-sdk/src/connector-runtime.ts:199)). You need a connection-level `syncRecords`/directory-sync lifecycle or an equivalent SCIM webhook path, not `insertEvent.afterPersist`. |

Against your recommendation as written, **5, 6, 11, and 12 fail outright**. Number 10 also fails unless the store and merge are assertion-aware. Number 1 becomes wrong on updates/deletions unless claim reconciliation is added. Numbers 2, 3, and 8 are covered only by the separately completed authz program, not by steps 1–5.

## C. OR semantics and columns

“Edges are inherently OR” is slightly too broad.

An edge is just a fact. The locked gate’s `EXISTS` over matching `can_read` edges gives allow edges OR semantics. Multiple `member_of` paths similarly expand the viewer closure. `deny_read` then overrides that union.

Therefore:

- “Do not model A AND B as two allow edges” is exactly right.
- “Compile intersections into effective principals” is exactly right.
- Row-level ACLs fit because the protected unit can be represented as a resource.
- A field inside an otherwise visible row is not a separate protected unit, so ordinary row edges cannot express it.

Your column-level diagnosis is right, but “projection mask after the gate” is insufficient. The mask must occur before every content-consuming seam, including indexing, embedding, prompt construction, derivation, export, caching, and logging. Splitting sensitive fields into separately ACL-gated facets is simpler and safer when the source schema permits it.

## D. Dropping the claims table

**Dropping a separate table can be correct. Dropping claim state is not. Your current recommendation drops both, so it is wrong.**

The simplest design consistent with “no new edge table” is to make `entity_relationships` assertion-granular:

```text
entity_relationships
  assertion_key text NOT NULL   -- server-generated, stable producer claim identity
  from_entity_id
  to_entity_id
  relationship_type_id
  source / confidence / metadata
  deleted_at
```

Then:

- Backfill existing rows with `legacy:<id>`.
- Replace live-triple uniqueness with live uniqueness on `(organization_id, assertion_key)`.
- Keep normal indexes on the logical triple.
- Multiple live rows with different assertion keys may represent the same logical edge.
- Ordinary graph reads use `EXISTS`; UI/list reads collapse logical duplicates and expose sources if useful.
- Retraction tombstones only the producer’s assertion.
- Connector assertion keys use stable source identity such as connection + feed + `origin_id` + rule ID—not `events.id`.
- `channel-about` config and manual assertions get different keys.
- Access-graph reconcile deletes only its own connection/compiler assertion keys.
- Merge repoints every surviving assertion; it no longer destroys a different producer merely because the logical triple collides.

This adds a column and changes the index, so it does amend the locked plan’s live-triple assumption and its “1 column + 2 tables” accounting ([authz plan §7](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:125)). That amendment must be explicit. If the budget and live-triple index are absolutely immovable, then the relationship-claims table has to come back. There is no design that can perform independent retraction without storing independent ownership somewhere.

## E. Simplest design covering all 12

1. **One claim-aware relationship store.**  
   It owns atomic assert, retract, source-scoped reconcile, merge/repoint, symmetric canonicalization, type-pair validation, tenant/public-target rules, confidence, and transaction propagation. All direct SQL mutations migrate to it.

2. **One protected security capability.**  
   Generic callers—including `$links`, auto-linker, custom connectors, and domain relationship rules—cannot assert or alter `member_of`, `can_read`, or `deny_read`. Only server-selected, audited ACL/directory compilers receive the internal capability. A connector merely self-declaring `aclSupport: full` must not qualify.

3. **Two connector lanes.**

   - Event-kind domain rules resolve named endpoints and reconcile stable relationship assertions from `origin_id`.
   - Trusted authz record sync emits `principal|identity|membership|acl`, including a feedless connection-level lifecycle for Okta/SCIM.

   The existing transactional `afterPersist` hook is a suitable commit seam—it runs on unchanged as well as newly persisted events ([insert-event.ts:416](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/insert-event.ts:416), [insert-event.ts:625](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/entity-slug-roundtrip/packages/server/src/utils/insert-event.ts:625))—but it needs the resolved endpoint-role map and stable source identity. Do not derive edges from the unordered `entity_ids` bag.

4. **Finish the locked gate unchanged in principle.**  
   Trusted membership closure, effective `can_read`, deny-wins, user ∩ agent, source freshness inside SQL, owner-only unsupported connectors, and all-source derived provenance. Arbitrary ERP `belongs_to`/`mentions` edges never enter authorization traversal.

5. **Normalize field ACLs into resource ACLs where possible.**  
   Base invoice event without `total_amount`; finance-only facet event containing it. Both can point at the same invoice entity, while only the facet carries the finance ACL resource. If arbitrary field masking is a hard product requirement, admit that it is a separate subsystem rather than pretending ordinary edges cover it.

That is the smallest coherent answer: **no new claims table, but one assertion key on the existing graph; one central capability boundary; two connector record lanes; the already-locked gate and provenance table; sensitive fields split into separately gated facets.**

Evidence boundary: I reviewed local `origin/main` at `5a653ab955a4ccdbfbdcac658520c490329b38a6`; every cited file is identical to that ref. Network DNS was blocked, so I could not independently prove the remote branch has not advanced past that SHA. No files were changed.
